space-symbol.context: An open box shape, a flat baseline with short upturned ends, that stands for a typed space. Used in word processors and code editors to show invisible space characters and in typography guides.

decimal-tab.context: Rows of numbers of different lengths with their decimal points lined up on one dashed vertical line. Used for decimal tab stops in word processors and for lining up prices and figures in columns.

justify-all-lines.context: Justified text lines where the short last line is stretched to full width by arrows pointing outward. Used for the force justify setting that spreads every line, including the final one, edge to edge.

vertical-justification.context: A text frame whose lines are spread evenly from top to bottom, with a double headed vertical arrow beside it. Used for vertical justification and distributing lines to fill the full height of a text box.

align-to-spine.context: An open book with the text lines on both pages sitting against the centre fold. Used for the align to spine paragraph setting in page layout tools for books and facing pages.

widows-and-orphans.context: Two page outlines where one lone short line sits at the top of the second page. Used for widow and orphan control, the setting that stops single stranded lines at page breaks.

keep-with-next.context: A heading bar and paragraph lines tied together by a chain link. Used for the keep with next paragraph setting that stops a heading from being left alone at the bottom of a page.

keep-lines-together.context: A block of text lines held as one group by a bracket on its left side. Used for the keep lines together setting that prevents a paragraph from splitting across a page break.

line-length.context: Lines of body text with a horizontal dimension arrow measuring the width of one full line. Used for line length, measure and column width settings and for readability and characters per line guidance.

text-rivers.context: A justified paragraph with a wavy blank channel running down through the gaps between words. Used to flag rivers, the distracting white streaks that appear in poorly spaced justified text.

text-frame.context: A dashed rectangle with square handles at its corners and a capital T inside. Used for the text frame or text box tool in layout and design programs.

threaded-text-frames.context: Two dashed text boxes joined by a curved arrow so text flows from the first into the second. Used for linked or threaded text frames in magazine and book layout.

overset-text.context: A text box full of lines with a small plus marker at its lower corner. Used to show overset text, content that does not fit in its frame and is hidden.

shrink-text-to-fit.context: A narrow text box holding a capital A with arrows pressing in from both sides. Used for shrink text on overflow, autofit and scale to fit options.

span-columns.context: A wide heading bar stretching across two columns of text lines below it. Used for the span columns paragraph setting that lets a heading cross every column.

column-break.context: Two text columns where the first stops early at a dashed break line and the second keeps going. Used for the column break command that pushes following text into the next column.

page-border.context: A page outline with a second decorative frame drawn inside its edge. Used for page borders on certificates, invitations and printed documents.

anchored-image.context: A picture frame beside lines of text with a small anchor tying it to the paragraph. Used for anchored objects that move with their text when a document is edited.

wrap-top-and-bottom.context: A full width picture block with text lines only above and below it. Used for the top and bottom text wrap option that keeps text from sitting beside an image.

wrap-behind-text.context: A dashed picture block sitting beneath text lines that run straight across it. Used for the behind text wrap option, watermarks and background images.

wrap-in-front-of-text.context: A solid picture block covering the middle of several text lines. Used for the in front of text wrap option where an object sits on top of the text.

wrap-tight.context: A round picture with text lines that stop close around its curved edge. Used for tight or contour text wrap that follows the outline of an image or shape.

inline-image.context: A short line of text with a small picture frame set into it like a word. Used for inline images, pictures that sit in the text line and move with it.

bleed-area.context: A page with a dashed bleed line outside its trim edge and artwork running past the trim. Used in print design for bleed settings and print ready files.

page-imposition.context: A press sheet divided into eight page panels with the top row turned upside down. Used for imposition, the arrangement of pages on a printing sheet before folding and cutting.

perfect-binding.context: A book block with a thick glued spine edge and stacked page lines. Used for perfect binding, the glued spine finish on paperbacks, catalogues and magazines.

multilevel-list.context: An outline list with numbered entries at two indent levels, a main item and numbered sub items beneath it. Used for multilevel lists, legal numbering and nested outlines.

lettered-list.context: Three list lines each led by the small letters a, b and c. Used for alphabetical lists, lettered sub points and outlines.

roman-numeral-list.context: Three list lines led by the roman numerals I, II and III. Used for outlines, legal documents, chapters and formal numbered lists.

definition-list.context: Heavy term bars each followed by an indented description line. Used for definition lists, glossaries and key and value descriptions.

dash-list.context: Three list lines each led by a short dash. Used for dash bulleted lists and informal lists in notes and documents.

toggle-list.context: List lines led by small solid triangles, one turned down above indented lines. Used for collapsible lists, toggle blocks and disclosure outlines in notes apps.

restart-numbering.context: Numbered lines followed by a circular arrow and a new line numbered 1. Used for the restart numbering command that starts a numbered list over at one.

bullet-point.context: A single solid round bullet beside a short text line. Used for bullet points, unordered lists and list markers.

arrow-bullet-list.context: Three list lines each led by a small arrowhead bullet. Used for arrow bulleted lists, feature lists and call out points.

alphabetical-order.context: The letters A and Z stacked with a downward arrow beside them. Used for sorting from A to Z and ordering lists and tables alphabetically.

cell-alignment.context: A table cell with text lines centred inside its border. Used for cell alignment options such as centring text horizontally and vertically in a table cell.

cell-padding.context: A table cell with a dashed inner box showing the space between its content and its border. Used for cell padding and cell margin settings in tables and web layout.

draw-table.context: A small table grid whose last border line is still being drawn by a pencil. Used for the draw table tool that sketches a table by dragging lines.

text-to-table.context: Text lines, an arrow and a small table grid showing plain text turned into a table. Used for convert text to table commands in word processors.

distribute-columns.context: A table with three equal columns and an even spacing scale above them. Used for the distribute columns evenly command that gives every column the same width.

diagonal-cell-split.context: A table corner cell crossed by a diagonal line with a text mark in each half. Used for diagonal header cells in matrix style tables that label both a row and a column.

repeat-header-row.context: The same heavy header row repeated at the top of a table piece on the next page. Used for the repeat header rows setting for tables that run across pages.

split-table.context: A table grid cut into two parts with a dashed cut line between them. Used for the split table command that breaks one table into two.

table-gridlines.context: A table drawn in dotted lines with no solid borders. Used for the show gridlines option that reveals the cell structure of a table without printed borders.

erase-table-border.context: A small table grid with an eraser wiping out part of an inner line. Used for the eraser tool that removes table borders and merges cells.

tab-leader.context: A short word, a row of dots and a number joined by a dotted leader. Used for tab leaders in tables of contents, menus and price lists.

table-of-figures.context: A list of small picture thumbnails each followed by a dotted leader and a page number. Used for tables of figures and lists of illustrations in reports and books.

comment-thread.context: Two stacked speech bubbles joined by a thin bracket line so the second reads as a reply. Used for comment threads and replies in document review.

inline-comment.context: A text line with a highlighted word and a small speech bubble above it. Used for comments attached to a specific word or phrase in a document.

suggest-edits.context: Text with a crossed out word and a pencil writing a replacement above it. Used for suggesting mode and track changes where edits are proposed instead of applied.

change-bar.context: Text lines with a thick bar in the margin beside two of them. Used for change bars and revision marks that show which lines were modified.

stet-mark.context: A word with a dotted underline and a small scribbled note in the margin. Used for the stet proofreading mark that tells an editor to let the original text stand.

transpose-mark.context: Two letters with an S shaped proofreading curve looping over one and under the other. Used for the transpose mark that swaps the order of letters or words.

insert-space-mark.context: A text line with a caret mark below it and a hash sign above it. Used for the proofreading mark that says a space must be added at that point.

capitalize-proof-mark.context: A lowercase letter with three short lines under it. Used as the proofreading mark that asks for a letter to be set as a capital.

lowercase-proof-mark.context: A capital letter crossed by a single diagonal slash. Used as the proofreading mark that asks for a capital letter to be changed to lowercase.

endnote.context: A document page with a short rule near the bottom and a numbered note beneath it. Used for endnotes and footnotes that hold references and citations.

cross-reference.context: Two text blocks with a curved arrow from a small number in one to a heading in the other. Used for cross references that link a mention to the section it points to.

comments-sidebar.context: A page of text with a column of small speech bubbles along its right side. Used for the comments pane that lists review notes next to the document.

mark-as-final.context: A document with a small ribbon seal at its lower corner. Used for the mark as final command that flags a document as finished and read only.

errata-slip.context: A narrow slip of paper with two lines tucked between the pages of an open book. Used for errata slips, loose corrections inserted into printed books.

em-dash.context: A long dash standing between two upright letter strokes. Used for the em dash punctuation mark that sets off a break in a sentence.

en-dash.context: A medium dash between the digits 1 and 9 as a number range. Used for the en dash punctuation mark that marks ranges of numbers, dates and pages.

interpunct.context: A single dot at mid letter height between two letters. Used for the interpunct or middle dot that separates words or syllables.

apostrophe.context: A small curved comma shaped mark raised high beside the letter s. Used for apostrophes in possessives and contractions.

full-stop.context: A solid round dot on the baseline after a short word. Used for the full stop or period that ends a sentence.

smart-quotes.context: Curly double quotation marks next to a pair of straight vertical quote marks. Used for smart quotes settings and for comparing typographic and straight quotes.

low-quotation-marks.context: A comma shaped double quote at the baseline on one side and a raised pair on the other. Used for low opening quotation marks in German and other languages.

cjk-corner-brackets.context: A pair of East Asian quotation brackets shaped like an upper left and a lower right corner. Used for Japanese and Chinese quotations and titles.

irony-mark.context: A backwards question mark with its hook opening to the left. Used for the irony mark, a rare punctuation sign for sarcasm and rhetorical questions.

dinkus.context: Three asterisks spaced in a row. Used for the dinkus, an ornament that marks a section or scene break in writing.

grave-accent.context: A lowercase e with a short stroke slanting down to the right above it. Used for the grave accent diacritic in French, Italian and other languages.

caron.context: A lowercase c with a small v shaped mark above it. Used for the caron or hacek diacritic found in Czech, Slovak and other Slavic alphabets.

dot-above.context: A capital I with a single round dot above it. Used for the dot above diacritic, as in the Turkish capital dotted I.

dotless-i.context: A lowercase i stem without its dot beside a normal dotted i for comparison. Used for the dotless i found in Turkish and Azeri writing.

solidus.context: A forward slash between the digits 1 and 2. Used for the solidus or fraction slash, the slanted line in fractions and alternatives.

block-selection.context: Text lines with a tall column shaped selection box cutting across them. Used for block or column selection that selects a rectangle of text instead of whole lines.

overtype-mode.context: Letters either side of a solid block cursor covering one letter. Used for overtype or overwrite mode where typing replaces existing characters.

vertical-text-cursor.context: A sideways I beam cursor beside columns of vertical text marks. Used for the vertical text tool and cursor in design programs and for top to bottom writing.
